newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore says seizes cannabis worth US$21 million.
newsitem.headline: Singapore says seizes cannabis worth US$21 million.

text.p: Singapore authorities said on Tuesday they had seized cannabis worth some Singapore $30 million (US$21 million) from a cargo ship in the city state's harbour.

The Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB) said the 4.3 tonnes of cannibis, thought to be headed for Europe, was discovered in packing cases in a container on the cargo ship "Mint Zoom" by sniffer dogs on Sunday, CNB Deputy Director Tan Seck Keng said.
The ship, said to be carrying fabric and garments to Vietnam from Cambodia, was considered by CNB officers to be following an unusual route.
"This was clearly an attempt to cover tracks and the point of origin of this ship," Tan said.

Authorities said they began monitoring one of the world's busiest ports after receiving reports that several recent drug shipments seized in Western countries appeared to have been routed via Singapore.
No arrests have been made but an investigation was being conducted. The CNB said it had not identified any suspects.

"This container originated outside Singapore and the people we need to question are outside our jurisdiction too," said Tan, adding that the CNB was liaising with foreign drug enforcement agencies on the case.

Singapore has tough anti-drug laws including a mandatory death sentence for anyone aged over 18 years found guilty of trafficking more than 15 grams (half an ounce) of heroin, 30 grams (an ounce) of morphine or 500 grams (18 ounces) of cannabis.
Of the more than 280 people hanged for various crimes in Singapore since 1975, about half have been for drug-related offences.
